author: Isaac Dunn
title: Supervised finetuning on low-harm reward hacking generalises to high-harm reward hacking
snippet: Supervised finetuning may be a poor proxy for the training that models will actually undergo. Future work might use training that is closer to real training to obtain stronger evidence about the reward hacking generalisation that we should expect in practice. The simplest step up would be to use a type of “expert iteration”: rather than doing supervised finetuning on specifically-created “golden” examples of reward hacking, instead sample from the model, and then train on the high-reward samples.
statement: Test whether reward hacking generalisation from low to high harm occurs under expert iteration instead of supervised finetuning.
group_statement: Rerun reward-hacking generalization experiments using RL methods (PPO, DPO, expert iteration, on-policy RL) instead of supervised fine-tuning.
